To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a simple method to enhance the performance of organic transistors by using topography-guided spreading of solution-processed organic semiconductors.
the mobility of solution- processed 6,13- bis (triisopropyl silylethynyl) -pentacene can be enhanced by more than a two-fold by the unidirectional topographic inkjet printing of a polymer insulator.
the mobility of the TIPS-Pentacene film is enhanced by more than a two-fold factor by the topography-guided anisotropic spreading of the TIPS- Pentacene solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the enhancement of the charge-carrier mobility by controlling the morphology and structure of the organic semiconductors.
the development of a novel method to enhance the field-effect mobility by UT of a polymer insulator, which is a promising approach to realize high-performance organic field-effect transitors.
a new concept of UT-based solution-processed field-effect transisters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the UT-dictating anisotropic drying process of TIPS-pentcane droplet is a promising method to enhance the field-effect mobility.
the UT-based approach to mobility enhancement is easily and widely applicable to different classes and types of soluble organic field effect transistors.
UT is an efficient approach for mobility enhancement of solution-processed organic semiconductor films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UT of a polymer insulator is an effective and facile way to enhance the mobility of organic field-effect transitors.
UT of a polymer insulator can be used to control the morphology of the solution-processed organic semiconductors and to enhance the field-effect mobilities of the organic field-effect transitors.
UT of an ink-printed insulator provides a simple and effective method to control the spreading and drying of solution-processed semiconducting materials, leading to an enhanced field-effect mobility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the UT of a polymer insulator can be used to tailor the morphology and hence the field-effect mobility in the solution-processed organic semiconductors.

the UT-based anisotropic wetted TIPS-pentace films can be a viable alternative to the more expensive and complex approaches such as the thermal evaporation, and the solution-processed self-assembled monolayers for the field-effect transisters with high mobilities.
UT of a polymer insulator can be used as a simple yet effective method to improve the field-effect mobility in solution-processed organic field-effect transitors.
